name: Cooinda
reason: Settlement and lodge; a pick-up point, not a place to do or see anything (rule 2/3: wrapper, the draws are Yellow Water and Warradjan, both listed).
objection: Wikivoyage and Parks Australia both name it as the hub on the route; but it is a lodge/base, and a base is the destination's job.

name: Gunbalanya
reason: Community reached by permit; the visitor draws are Injalak Arts and Injalak Hill, listed separately (rule 3: a town is not a spot beside its own attraction).
objection: Wikipedia has 15k views and tours go there; but the only counted source is the Injalak tour page, so the town is a wrapper.

name: Nourlangie Rock
reason: Wikivoyage See > Rock art lists it; Parks Australia and NT Tourism too (rule 1, 3 sources). Rock art galleries, 1 km walk, an obvious draw (rule 2).
objection: Could be treated as part of the Burrungkuy area with Nawurlandja and Anbangbang; but it is the headline site and the others are separate trailheads.

name: Nanguluwur Art Site
reason: Wikivoyage See > Rock art lists it with description; Parks Australia too; 2 sources, its own walk and a distinct gallery.
objection: Zero page views and a long dirt road; a second-tier rock art site that few visit. Wikivoyage still singles it out.

name: Twin Falls
reason: Wikivoyage See > Waterfalls and Parks Australia; boat shuttle then walk, a headline Kakadu sight.
objection: Seasonal and 4WD access; still a permanent place visitors reach on tours.

name: Gunlom
reason: Wikivoyage lists Gunlom Plunge Pool and Gunlom Falls, Parks Australia too; swim and climb with views, half a day.
objection: Far south, 200 km from Jabiru; distance is not a reason to reject.

name: Warradjan Aboriginal Cultural Centre
reason: Wikivoyage See > Visitor and cultural centres with hours, and Parks Australia gallery list; open to the public with exhibits (rule 2).
objection: A centre is a building and visits may be short; but exhibits and art make a 30+ min stop.

name: Mamukala Wetlands
reason: Parks Australia itinerary and NT Tourism top 10 name it; bird hide and loop, a recognised birdwatching stop.
objection: Seasonal (best late dry season); permanent venue, so allowed.

name: Nawurlandja Lookout
reason: One counted source (Parks Australia), short climb lookout next to Nourlangie; case for: popular sunset viewpoint with its own walk; against: part of the Burrungkuy area, short.
objection: Rule 3: a lookout on a track next to a listed spot is part of it; but Parks gives it its own walk entry.

name: Cahills Crossing
reason: Parks Australia things-do and 5-day itinerary name it as the croc-spotting stop; a recognised wildlife and tidal causeway sight.
objection: Roadside stop of 15-30 min; but a guide singles it out, so it passes the roadside rule.

name: Mirrai Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage and Parks Australia; 3.6 km return walk to a lookout over the escarpment, its own trailhead near Bowali.
objection: Distinct from Mirray Lookout (near Ubirr); a mid-tier walk with zero page views.

name: Bardedjilidji Walk
reason: Wikivoyage calls it one of Kakadu's most interesting short walks; Parks itinerary also; 2.5 km, 2 hours.
objection: Close to Cahills Crossing and Ubirr; but its own walk and sandstone formations.

name: Manngarre Rainforest Walk
reason: Two Parks itineraries name it; 1.2 km wheelchair-friendly rainforest walk, 20-30 min. For: accessible, in itineraries. Against: very short and only in itineraries, no description in a guide.
objection: Counted sources are Parks itineraries only; could be seen as a boat ramp stroll.

name: Gubara Pools
reason: Wikivoyage describes the 6 km return walk to pools with a swim, allow 4 hours; a worthwhile half-day walk.
objection: Single counted source; but a clear description of a full activity.

name: Barrk Sandstone Walk
reason: Wikivoyage and Parks list the 12 km, 6-8 hour walk, a long walk with its own trailhead and sandstone country.
objection: Overlaps Nourlangie lookout track at the start; the long walk is a distinct activity.

name: Yurmikmik Walks
reason: Wikivoyage names the series of walks (Boulder Creek, Motor Car Falls); one source. For: a walking area; against: overlaps Motor Car Falls (kept) and is a group of trails not one place.
objection: A grouping of walks rather than a place; could be merged with Motor Car Falls.

name: Kungarre Walk
reason: Two Parks sources (itinerary and things-do); 3.6 km walk to a billabong with birdlife at South Alligator.
objection: Zero views; second-tier walk. Itinerary inclusion supports it.

name: Home Billabong
reason: NT Tourism top 10 things in Kakadu and Parks; viewing platform on a 1.8 km floodplain walk near Yellow Water.
objection: Close to Yellow Water, and may be seen as part of that area; its separate walk and platform make it distinct.

name: Nadab Lookout
reason: Lookout on the climb above Ubirr; part of the Ubirr visit (rule 3, part of a larger spot).
objection: Wikipedia has an article and Parks itinerary names it; but visitors reach it as the Ubirr walk.

name: Bukbukluk Lookout
reason: One counted source: Parks things-do menu only lists the walk, no description. Lookout in the south.
objection: Name only in a navigation menu; cannot confirm the visit length or access.

name: Budjmi Lookout
reason: Only a name in the Parks walks menu, no description; a short lookout walk with no guide singling it out (rule 1/3).
objection: Parks does name it, but only as a menu item.

name: Mirray Lookout
reason: Only a name in the Parks walks menu; short lookout near Ubirr, part of that area (rule 3).
objection: Wikipedia article exists, but no counted source describes it.

name: Mardukal Billabong
reason: Name only in the Parks nav (walk and billabong lists), no description; minor billabong walk.
objection: Parks lists it twice; still no visitor-facing content.

name: Kungardun Walk
reason: Name only in the Parks walks menu, no description or distinct draw.
objection: Parks names it; but no information to confirm a half-hour draw.

name: Yilikadjarr Walk
reason: Name only in the Parks walks menu, no description.
objection: Same as Kungardun.

name: Bubba Wetlands Walk
reason: Name only in the Parks walks menu, no description.
objection: A wetlands walk could be a good bird stop; nothing sourced says so.

name: Barrk Marlam Walk
reason: Name only in the Parks walks menu, no description; near the Barrk Sandstone Walk area.
objection: Parks names it; but near-duplicate area of Barrk Sandstone Walk.

name: Badbong Wodjmeng Sandstone River Walk
reason: Name only in the Parks walks menu, no description.
objection: Could be a real river walk; nothing sourced describes it.

name: Bowali Track
reason: Name only in the Parks walks menu; a short track from the Bowali Visitor Centre, part of that spot (rule 3).
objection: Parks names it; but it is the visitor centre's own track.

name: Jim Jim Billabong
reason: Name only in the Parks birdwatching menu; no description; birdwatching spot beside Jim Jim access.
objection: Birdwatching sites are legitimate stops; but nothing sourced says what a visitor does.

name: Alligator Billabong
reason: Name only in the Parks birdwatching menu, no description.
objection: As Jim Jim Billabong.

name: Red Lily Billabong
reason: Name only in the Parks birdwatching menu, camping area billabong, no description.
objection: Known birding spot in reality; only one menu mention in the sources.

name: Bucket Billabong
reason: Name only in the Parks birdwatching menu, camping area billabong, no description.
objection: As Red Lily Billabong.

name: Marrawuddi Arts & Culture
reason: One counted source (Parks galleries list); gallery in Jabiru, open to visit. For: art centre listed by Parks; against: a gallery/shop, one source.
objection: Close to being a shop (rule 2).

name: Injalak Hill
reason: Parks cultural tour page: x-ray rock art hill reached only on Traditional Owner-guided tours from Injalak Arts, via permit. For: real rock art draw. Against: tour-only, one source, no open access (rule 2).
objection: The tour is the way in; per the vehicle/operator rule the place is the spot, but it is not freely accessible.

name: Roy Marika Lookout
reason: One counted source (NT Tourism Nhulunbuy bucket list): summit lookout a short walk from town with views over wetlands and harbour. For: the region's overview point; against: one source, short stop.
objection: A lookout over a town; ten-minute look.

name: Gayngaru Wetlands
reason: One NT Tourism source: paperbark walk with bird hides and platforms in town, culturally significant. For: distinct nature walk; against: single source, local park in town.
objection: Could be a local reserve rather than a tourist stop; tourism board does list it.

name: Wirrwawuy
reason: NT Tourism bucket list: sand dunes at Cape Wirrawoi for sunrise and sunset photographs, 5 km from town; second-tier beach/dune stop a source names.
objection: Near-duplicate of the nearby beach stretch (Middle Beach, Galuru) and a single source.

name: Middle Beach
reason: A plain stretch of beach between Wirrwawuy and Galuru; near-duplicate of those two (rule 3).
objection: Tourism board names it for family walks and fishing; but no distinct draw.

name: Galuru (East Woody Beach)
reason: Wikivoyage Arnhem Land and NT Tourism both name it: white sand, rust-red cliffs, sunset; 2 sources.
objection: Overlap with Dhamitjinya, its walk-out point; the beach is the access and a distinct place.

name: Dhamitjinya (East Woody Island)
reason: Wikivoyage Arnhem Land and NT Tourism: sandspit walk to an island with 360-degree views; 2 sources.
objection: Tidal access and shares a beach with Galuru; but a distinct walk-out destination.

name: Gadalathami (Town Beach)
reason: One NT source: nearest beach for evening strolls. For: in town, free; against: a local beach with no distinct draw, one source.
objection: A town beach locals use.

name: Garanhan (Macassan Beach)
reason: NT Tourism: Yolngu stone pictures of Macassan trade, picnic tables, 35 min from Nhulunbuy; distinct historic site.
objection: Single source and camping needs a permit; the day visit is open.

name: Banambarrna (Rainbow Cliffs)
reason: NT Tourism: 40 m coloured laterite cliffs, viewed from the beach; the top is closed as sacred, so visiting is from below.
objection: Single source; a roadside-ish stop of half an hour.

name: Bremer Island
reason: NT Tourism: day cruises and flights to a beach island; the place the cruise goes to is the spot (COVERAGE: island).
objection: Single source; needs boat or air and resort access; day cruises exist.

name: Lonely Beach (Bawaka Homelands)
reason: Reached only with a tour or permit on private homelands; not open to the public (rule 2).
objection: NT Tourism names it; but private access via an operator.

name: Victoria Settlement
reason: One NT Tourism source: 1838 British outpost ruins at Port Essington, boat or tour. For: a real historic site; against: remote, tour/permit access, one source.
objection: Heritage ruins with a difficult access.

name: Black Point Cultural Centre
reason: One NT Tourism source: ranger station and cultural centre at Black Point; cultural history. For: the park's visitor point; against: remote, permit-limited, one source.
objection: Staffed? Not confirmed; remote.

name: Umbakumba Art Centre
reason: One counted source (Wikivoyage Arnhem Land): art centre on Groote Eylandt. Against: remote island, permit constraints, no hours confirmed.
objection: A single-line listing.

name: Maningrida
reason: NT Tourism destination page (found by search) names the community, its arts centre and fishing; permit from the Northern Land Council. For: a gateway with an arts centre; against: the sight is the arts centre and the fishing, not the town (rule 3), permit needed.
objection: Town as wrapper of its attraction; the earlier script found no counted source.

name: Bowali Visitor Centre
reason: (auto-keep) Wikivoyage See > Visitor and cultural centres; Parks Australia; exhibits and gallery, open daily, free. Confirmed by search: hours 9-5 dry, 10-4 wet.
objection: A visitor centre can be a short stop; the walk-through display and gallery make it 30+ min.

name: Groote Eylandt
reason: (auto-keep downgraded) One counted source (Wikivoyage Arnhem Land); island with fishing and cave paintings, permit needed for land outside communities. For: an island named by guides; against: little for a casual visitor, permit logistics, one source.
objection: Remote island of about 1,500 km2; access by SeaLink-run flight and permit.
